newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended a quiet day's trading with mixed results as low volumes forced frustrated market players to look forward to U.S. data on Tuesday.
The January 2006 bond mirrored the performance of German Bund futures, finishing slightly weaker after being solidly higher at one stage in morning trading.
But the 5.75 percent February 2007 government, issued two weeks ago to become the new 10-year benchmark in guilders, ended slightly higher.
A dealer said data showing a fall in U.S. December existing home sales was not bad when compared with estimates.
"But the market failed to go up," he said.
Dealers said the market was more interested in U.S. fourth quarter employment cost data on Tuesday as well as bids for the balance of the new German Bund auction the same day.
"It could be quite important," said a trader. Another dealer said Dutch guilder paper tracked bunds as they gyrated through the day, with most trading action seen in the February 2007.
Data showing the strongest January rise in Dutch consumer confidence in 10 years failed to illicit much interest.
